rationale: The Agreement contains no Vendor-side audit, inspection, records-examination or verification right binding Mortgage Logic.com. Literal searches for "audit," "inspect," "records," "verif" and "monitor" return zero hits, and every provision in the areas where such a right would sit points the other way: § 6 (p0047) runs in Client's favour, entitling Client to documentation supporting amounts charged and to contest charges; § 3(e) (p0037) gives Client — not TrueLink — real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files; § 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client) contains only compliance, access-restriction and content warranties. The sole TrueLink self-help right, § 8(f) (p0058), permits TrueLink to implement technical mechanisms on its own hosted platform against spamming or illegal activity — platform policing, not an audit of Client's usage, and it confers no access to Client systems or records. § 9 obliges Client only to provide reasonable access for TrueLink's Y2K remediation at TrueLink's sole cost, which benefits us. rationale:
Compliant: the agreement imposes no non-solicitation, no-hire, or employee-inducement covenant on Mortgage Logic.com (Client), which is precisely our preferred position of "no non-solicit on Customer."

Scope of review. Section 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client) is the natural home for a customer-side covenant and is exhausted by unrelated obligations: compliance with laws (8(a)), notification (8(b)), limitation on access (8(c)), Credit Data licensing (8(d)), content representations (8(e)), and spamming (8(f)). Full-text searches for "solicit", "solicitation", "employ", "employee", "induce", "hire", "recruit", "personnel", "staff", and "engage" returned only unsolicited-email/spam (§ 7), access control (§ 8(c)), indemnity boilerplate (§ 12), and a trademark-search obligation (§ 2) — none of which restrict either party's hiring.

They constrain the content of a non-solicit only where one exists. These checks cannot be satisfied without first inserting a non-solicit into the agreement; doing so would manufacture a restrictive covenant against our own client and is a directionally wrong edit that is strictly worse than the current bargain.
